rounds.note: Round 1 closes the three real coverage holes the review found around B185 — the mobile seam's happy path (#0), the API's accuracy persistence via a recordLocation service spec plus `driverLocation` in the shared Prisma mock (#1, Opus), and the R3 negative-value pins on the DTO (#2) — and takes the one code hardening that sits on the rewritten line (#3: an implausible speed maps to null instead of 400ing the whole ping, server bound untouched). Gate finding #8 is disputed: the mobile jest command only fails on baseline because its target is this run's red-set file, and it passes post-change. All nine fixes run in a single wave; build-plan.md is shared by #1/#7/#9 and location-payload.test.ts by #0/#3, so they sit together.

Round 2 has a single upheld finding (#0, upper-bound speed guard). The current location-payload.ts already maps a converted speed above MAX_SPEED_KPH=500 to null (never clamped), so the round makes no logic change: the executor confirms the guard matches the excerpt (restoring it verbatim only if it has drifted) and pins it with boundary unit tests in apps/mobile/__tests__/location-payload.test.ts (200 m/s -> null, 500/3.6 -> ~500 passes, just above -> null, Infinity/NaN -> null). The API DTO's @Max(500) is untouched, the -1 sentinel mapping and accuracy handling are untouched, and api-before-OTA ordering is unaffected. One wave, Sonnet route.

confirmedFindings.summary: No test exercises buildLocationPayload with a valid (non-negative) heading or speed, so the m/s→km/h conversion and the pass-through branch are entirely unasserted.
confirmedFindings.detail: The suite passes exactly three inputs: {heading:-1, speed:-1} (asserts null/null), {accuracy:4.5} (asserts accuracy only), {accuracy:-1} (asserts accuracy only). Neither of the last two asserts heading or speedKph at all. Therefore a body of `const heading = null; const speedKph = null;` — or one that drops the `* 3.6` factor, or uses `/ 3.6` — passes all 3 tests green. Verified by reading the full test file; I ran `cd apps/mobile && npx jest location-payload.test` (3 passed). Concretely: a driver moving at 10 m/s should produce speedKph 36 and heading 90 should pass through as 90; nothing in the suite would catch a regression that returns null for both, which would silently strip heading/speed from every live-map breadcrumb while the red gate stays green.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add one non-REG case to the same describe: buildLocationPayload({latitude:34.05, longitude:-118.24, heading:90, speed:10}, ISO) → expect({heading:90, speedKph:36}). Assert as a pair so both wrong values surface, matching the style of the existing REG test.

T3/T4/T5 all live in apps/api/src/drivers/dto/post-location.dto.spec.ts and are pure `validate(plainToInstance(PostLocationDto, ...))` calls — they never touch drivers.service.ts. I confirmed by grep that `recordLocation` appears in no *.spec.ts anywhere under apps/api/src, and by running `cd apps/api && npx jest src/drivers --runInBand` (2 suites / 24 tests, all green with the line present). Failure scenario: change line 114 to `accuracy: dto.batteryPct`, or delete it entirely, and every test in the repo still passes — the column silently stays NULL for every ping, and R4 ships unverified. bug-test-plan.md's harness note already records the enabling gap (`driverLocation` is absent from apps/api/src/testing/prisma-mock.ts's allModels(), so a service-level spec would throw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'create')`) and deliberately fenced it out.

confirmedFindings.summary: R3 / acceptance criterion 3 — "a present negative heading/speedKph is still rejected" — has no test; the only heading values in any API spec are `null` and `180`.
confirmedFindings.detail: The T5 pin block covers a fully valid payload, lat/lng over and under range, and a missing recordedAt. It never sends a negative heading or speedKph. I grepped every *.spec.ts under apps/api/src for `heading`: the only two hits are post-location.dto.spec.ts:34 (`heading: null`) and :65 (`heading: 180`). Failure scenario: someone later 'fixes' B185 the tempting server-side way by deleting `@Min(0)` from heading and speedKph (post-location.dto.ts:20 and :27) — the DTO then accepts the raw iOS `-1` sentinel and writes heading=-1 / speedKph=-1 to DriverLocation, and the whole suite stays green. That server-side relaxation is precisely the alternative the cause-ruling rejected and that R3 exists to forbid, so the requirement's only guard is currently a comment.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add two cases to the T5 pin block: `{...basePayload, heading: -1}` and `{...basePayload, speedKph: -1}`, each asserting an error on that property whose constraints contain `min`. Mirror the existing lat/lng assertion shape.

confirmedFindings.summary: The speed conversion has no upper guard, so a GPS speed above ~138.9 m/s still 400s the entire ping on the DTO's @Max(500) — the same silent-total-loss failure mode B185 fixes, on the opposite bound.
confirmedFindings.detail: `coords.speed * 3.6` is passed through unclamped, while post-location.dto.ts:29 carries `@Max(500)` on speedKph. A glitched fix reporting speed 200 m/s yields speedKph 720, the DTO rejects the request, and location-tracker.native.ts:19-24's empty catch swallows the 400 — lat/lng are lost for that sample with no error anywhere, exactly the B185 symptom. This is PRE-EXISTING (the replaced inline expression did the same `* 3.6` with no clamp) and build-plan.md's non-goals explicitly fence out plausibility checks as 'hardening, not a bug', so this is reported for the record, not as a required change — but it sits on the one line this fix rewrote and leaves the ping-loss class only half closed.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: If taken: decide between clamping speedKph to the DTO's 500 ceiling, mapping an implausible speed to null (consistent with the sentinel treatment), or leaving it and filing a registry row. Do not change the server bound.

confirmedFindings.summary: The stated rollback ("revert the diff") is unsafe in one direction the risk table does not cover: reverting the API alone after the mobile OTA ships makes forbidNonWhitelisted reject 100% of pings.
confirmedFindings.detail: The Risks table covers the forward ordering (mobile OTA before the API deploy) but the Rollback line says only "revert the diff; no schema/migration involved". After the fix, location-payload.ts:28 emits `accuracy` on essentially every valid fix (any non-negative device accuracy), and location-tracker.native.ts:37/:81 spread it into the POST body. main.ts:145-149 sets `forbidNonWhitelisted: true`. Failure scenario: the API PR merges and deploys, the mobile OTA ships, then the API is reverted for an unrelated reason — every ping from every updated device now fails whitelist validation on `accuracy` and is swallowed by the tracker's empty catch, turning B185's intermittent iOS-only gap into a total, silent loss of live tracking on both platforms. This is strictly worse than the pre-fix state and is the exact hazard the forward-ordering mitigation guards against, just in reverse.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: State in the rollback row (and the PR body) that the API's `accuracy` field must not be reverted while any shipped mobile build sends it — roll mobile back first, or leave the additive DTO field in place and revert only the mobile seam.
